originalText:
I have a keen interest in Spacetech. In fact, I have even invested in a solid Spacetech startup here in India (Will share more on that another day). The global focus today is on SpaceX’s IPO.

The reported numbers are very interesting
-Expected IPO price: $135/share
-Raise: ~$75B at  ~$1.75T valuation
-Demand: 3.5 to 4x oversubscribed
-Retail access: Up to 30% retail allocation

While the scale is massive, what genuinely excites me isn't just the size of the IPO. It is how and where the price discovery is happening. 

For decades, IPO pricing was a closed-door game controlled by bankers and a few privileged institutions.
But thanks to crypto rails, @SpaceX-linked perpetual futures have been trading publicly, 24/7, since mid-May.

Look at the public data:
– SPCX futures trading around $173.5 this morning vs. the $135 IPO price 
– A ~29% premium discovered before the bell even rings – Over $3.2B in cumulative volume and ~$390M in open interest.  

An important note: These are synthetic perps, not actual SpaceX shares (meaning no ownership or voting rights). But they prove an important point. Crypto markets are creating a live, liquid, and democratic signal of what the market actually thinks an asset is worth.

And the track record is honest, not perfect: Airbnb's futures undershot the 2020 pop. Coinbase's overshot at peak mania in 2021. But just last month, these markets called the Cerebras opening price within ~1.3%. As liquidity deepens, the signal sharpens. (Image generated via Claude Fable 5. In the comments)

Yes, three data points is a small sample. But the direction is unmistakable. We are shifting to an era where price discovery happens continuously, in public, weeks in advance! Later today, we find out how accurate the crowd's math is this time on SpaceX. 

But one thing is crystal clear: Price discovery is finally becoming public infrastructure and it will only get better when more people start participating in these global markets.
